summary: Configured node2 on VLAN 10 and node3 on VLAN 20 over the shared link (node1's eth1 / node2 & node3's enp8s0), with node1 (VyOS) as router-on-a-stick using 802.1q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24), plus a forward-filter firewall permitting inter-VLAN traffic. node2 got enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.2/24) via NetworkManager VLAN connection with a static route to 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.1; node3 got enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.2/24) with a static route to 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.1. Verified end-to-end reachability and confirmed via tcpdump that traffic is tagged 802.1Q vlan 10/20 on the shared link and routed by node1. All three nodes were then sequentially rebooted (one at a time, config persisted across reboot), each confirmed via changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, with full VLAN config and cross-VLAN connectivity re-verified after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected NIC layout on node1 (VyOS eth0/eth1), node2 (enp1s0/enp8s0), node3 (enp1s0/enp8s0) to identify the shared link

Configured VyOS node1: eth1 vif 10 (10.10.10.1/24), eth1 vif 20 (10.10.20.1/24), firewall ipv4 forward filter default-drop + accept rules for established/related and inter-VLAN traffic, committed and saved
Configured node2: nmcli VLAN connection enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.2/24), disabled DHCP on the raw enp8s0 profile, added static route to 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.1
Configured node3: nmcli VLAN connection enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.2/24), disabled DHCP on the raw enp8s0 profile, added static route to 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.1
Fixed a dual-default-route asymmetry (removed VLAN gateway, used subnet-specific static routes) that initially caused 'Destination Host Unreachable'
Verified end-to-end ping node2<->node3 through node1, and confirmed 802.1Q vlan 10/20 tagging via tcpdump -e on node1 eth1
Captured baseline boot_id and health/config state on all 3 nodes

Rebooted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time), polled each until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified VLAN interfaces, routes, firewall/forwarding, and end-to-end connectivity after each restart

evidence.requirement: node2 assigned to VLAN 10, node3 assigned to VLAN 20 over the shared link
evidence.summary: nmcli created enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.2/24) on node2 and enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.2/24) on node3, both up

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 (router-on-a-stick + firewall forward rules)
evidence.summary: VyOS eth1 vif 10/20 sub-interfaces and firewall ipv4 forward filter accept rules committed and saved in /config/config.boot

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other across VLANs via node1
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping succeeded (ttl=63, one hop through router) after fixing the default-route asymmetry with subnet-specific static routes

evidence.requirement: Traffic is actually 802.1Q-tagged as VLAN 10/20 on the shared link, not just IP-routed coincidentally
evidence.summary: tcpdump -e on node1's eth1 shows ICMP traffic tagged 'vlan 10' from node2 and 'vlan 20' to/from node3, confirming real VLAN segmentation and inter-VLAN routing

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 32669db3...; reboot issued; new boot_id 2355718c... confirms restart; post-restart VLAN interfaces, ip_forward=1, and pings to both node2/node3 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bf8b9d80...; reboot issued; new boot_id 8430558c... confirms restart; post-restart enp8s0.10 address, static route, and ping to node3 (10.10.20.2) succeeded

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b...; reboot issued; new boot_id 93170a47... confirms restart; post-restart enp8s0.20 address, static route, and ping to node2 (10.10.10.2) succeeded
